title: BandParity: the band-parity sum of a quartic character, two laws modulo 4
abstract: For a prime p = 5 (mod 8) let chi be the quartic Dirichlet character with chi(2) = i, with values in the Gaussian integers, and let C(p) = f + i e be the sum of chi(n) (-1)^floor(n^2/p) over 0 < n < p/2. The development proves that f = (p-1)/4 (mod 4) and e = kappa (mod 4) for every such p, where kappa is the sum of the Legendre symbols (n/p) over 0 < n < p/4. The mechanism is a matching lemma: for sign functions sigma, tau and a bijection pi, the correlation sum sigma(x) tau(pi x) is congruent modulo 4 to the sum of the two marginals minus the number of terms, so it does not depend on pi. Along the way it proves the parity dictionary (-1)^floor(n^2/p) = s(n) s(n^2) with s(x) = (-1)^<x>, the coset form f = sum over the fourth powers H of s(u) s(u^2) and e = the same sum over 2H, the lag identity sum over 2H of s(u) s(2u) = kappa exactly, the exact coset parities sum_H s = k + 2t and sum_{2H} s = t - 2k where B_{1,chi} = k + i t, and the Coordinate Congruence kappa = (p-1)/4 + k + t (mod 4). It also proves the odd-subgroup congruence: for an odd modulus N >= 3, a subgroup H of (Z/N)^x of odd order h, a coset X = xH and an even exponent e >= 2, the band-parity sum of X and -X over (0, N/2) equals sum over X of s(u) s(u^e) and is congruent to h - 2 alpha(X) - 2 alpha(X^e) modulo 4, where alpha counts elements with odd least residue.
